source: PROVISIONAL (sugars-24): FAO 2019 (ca5644en.pdf) Table 1 Group 2 p.11 "sugar and molasses obtained from cane or beet; honey extracted from combs and syrup from maple trees"; exact term not named by the clause (inference level: class-instance of sugar: misri is crystallised sugar candy made from sugar or palmyrah juice); bare "misri" only, plain form; blends, flavoured and mixed forms abstain or follow their markers. Identity: FSSAI naming only. FSSAI Chapter 2.8 Sweetening agents including honey (full PDF, https://www.fssai.gov.in/docs/food-law/regulations/compendium/food-products-standards/Chapter%202_8%20(Sweetening%20agents%20including%20Honey).pdf) defines "MISRI means the product made in the form of candy obtained from any kind of sugar or palmyrah juice" with total sugar not less than 98.0% by weight. Not encoded from the same chapter: golden syrup (made by inversion of sugar, and invert sugar is a Group 4 marker in this lexicon) and dried glucose syrup (glucose syrup is a Group 4 marker).
